title: The case against JPEG XL
summary: A critical analysis examining why JPEG XL, despite being technically superior to existing formats with better compression and lossless support, failed to gain adoption due to browser vendor politics, lack of industry support, and the rise of competing formats like AVIF. The article explores the complex dynamics of web standards and how technical merit alone isn't sufficient for technology adoption.
problem_solved: Documents and analyzes why a technically superior image format failed to achieve market adoption due to browser vendor politics and ecosystem fragmentation.
why_valuable: Provides valuable insights into how web standards decisions are made and why technically superior solutions can fail in the market due to corporate interests and timing.
